units: sigma/m in cm^2/g; velocities in km/s

conventions.maxwell: Model value is <sigma_V v^n>/<v^n> over f(v) ~ v^2 exp(-v^2/(4 sigma_1D^2)), with sigma_1D = sqrt(pi)/4 times mean_relative_velocity_kms and n = moment. n = 1 is the definition sigma/m = <sigma v>/(m <v>) of Sagunski et al. (arXiv:2006.12515, Eq. 6).
conventions.fixed: Model value is sigma_V(v) on a logarithmic grid over velocity_range_kms, combined with 'combine' (min is the conservative choice when the paper gives no single velocity).
conventions.sigma_V: Viscosity cross section normalised to equal the total cross section for isotropic scattering (Yang & Yu, arXiv:2205.03392, Eq. 2.5). All limits below were derived for velocity-independent isotropic scattering.

sets.default: Group and cluster core limits of Sagunski et al. and the revised merging-cluster limit of Wittman et al.
sets.stringent: default plus the tighter cluster limits (Andrade et al., Eckert et al., Harvey et al. 2019) and the Bullet Cluster limit of Randall et al.
sets.dwarf: Dwarf-galaxy limits only. They assume a velocity-independent cross section, depend on the halo modelling, and conflict with analyses that prefer 20-150 cm^2/g in the same class of galaxies (Correa, arXiv:2007.02958). Not part of any other set.

limits.label: Galaxy groups, core densities (Sagunski et al. 2021)
limits.notes: Limit with adiabatic contraction, adopted by the authors as conservative (0.9 for NFW only). Mean scattering velocity <v> = 4 sigma_0/sqrt(pi) of about 1150 km/s. Measured value 0.5 +- 0.2.

limits.label: Galaxy clusters, core densities (Sagunski et al. 2021)
limits.notes: Limit with adiabatic contraction (0.28 for NFW only). <v> = 4 sigma_0/sqrt(pi) of about 1900 km/s. Measured value 0.19 +- 0.09.

limits.label: Merging clusters, DM-galaxy offsets (Wittman et al. 2018)
limits.notes: The paper quotes 'relaxes the upper limit to <~ 2' (1.71 for the full sample, 2.27 for the reviewed subsample) and no collision velocity. The range 500-4000 km/s is the one Tulin & Yu (arXiv:1705.02358, Table I) assign to substructure mergers; the smallest model value in the range is used. Supersedes 0.47 of Harvey et al. 2015 (arXiv:1503.07675). The authors advise caution with this limit.

limits.label: Cluster strong lensing cores (Andrade et al. 2022)
limits.notes: Eight clusters with average relative velocity 1458 (+80 -81) km/s, defined as 4 sigma_0/sqrt(pi) for a Maxwellian. For a velocity-dependent model the authors interpret the result as a velocity-averaged transfer cross section.

limits.label: X-COP cluster density profiles (Eckert et al. 2022)
limits.notes: Quoted 'at collision velocity ~1000 km/s' without a definition; treated here as a mean relative velocity.

limits.label: BCG wobbles in cluster cores (Harvey et al. 2019)
limits.notes: The paper gives no velocity. 1500 km/s is the cluster-core velocity of Tulin & Yu (arXiv:1705.02358, Table I). The authors note the measured offsets are close to the simulation softening length.

limits.label: Bullet Cluster, DM-galaxy offset (Randall et al. 2008)
limits.notes: 68% CL. Randall et al. use the 4700 km/s shock velocity and test 3100 km/s; Robertson et al. (arXiv:1605.04307) find a halo relative velocity of 3900 km/s, call this constraint 'strongly overstated' and find sigma/m = 2 compatible with the observed offset. The 0.7 limit from the mass-to-light ratio is not used.

limits.label: Draco central density (Read et al. 2018)
limits.notes: 0.32 at 95% CL. The paper states no velocity; 58 km/s is the mean relative velocity Correa (arXiv:2007.02958) gives for Draco. The authors caution that the bound may not extrapolate to velocity-dependent cross sections. Correa prefers 20-30 cm^2/g for the same galaxy.

limits.label: Segue 1 (Hayashi et al. 2021)
limits.notes: The paper gives 'typical DM velocities of the UFDs, v = O(10) km/s' with v = 4 sigma_0/sqrt(pi); 10 km/s is used. The limits depend on priors and on the simple SIDM halo model.
